expectation: A standalone chat left in the store as a hidden board task is converted once into its own model: it keeps its ID so the existing conversation transcript stays attached, keeps its provider session, carries its in-flight turn state across with the status message and progress report that explain it, is removed from the board so it never lists or resolves as a task, and reopening the chat returns that same migrated chat rather than creating a second one.

Each standalone chat page is its own provider session: the first turn of a page starts a fresh session carrying the system prompt plus only that page's own turns, later turns on that page resume it without repeating the page context, and a different page never shares it, so an earlier page's turns never reach a later page. An annotation that quotes an earlier page carries just that page into the current turn, and rotating sessions still leaves every page's messages visible in the transcript.

The Chat button opens the standalone chat — its own model rather than a board task — in a sliding sidebar that never appears on the board, task commands cannot reach it by ID, and the bridge rejects any attempt to add a repository or worktree root to it. The GUI composer works without a configured repository parent and omits task status, repository controls, the Changes sidebar, and the no-repository-selected banner. Its CLI page close-turn signal keeps a continuing reply on the active page and starts a new titled page on a topic change, a completed turn's user and assistant messages persist onto the active page without leaking onto other pages, and pages are findable by search. Each page is also stored in a separate atomic JSON file in a discoverable archive directory; pages already present before file archiving are backfilled once, and each file tracks current metadata and messages. A turn that omits close-turn is tracked as missed, then a background low-effort Luna fallback rejects one malformed classification and retries, moves both messages to its correctly titled page, keeps page evaluation visually quiet while the primary answer remains usable, then updates the transcript separator with the title when classification completes; a following send waits for that decision, and preserves chronological order on a later append. An explicit page start during a pending fallback cancels its stale result, keeps the missed turn on its original page, and clears the warning. If all helper results are invalid, the pending decision remains durable, blocks the next provider send, and retries after the helper recovers; the UI keeps the unresolved state visually quiet and sends successfully once recovery completes. Earlier pages stay visible in the transcript after their page session rotates, and a board task conversation rejects a chat page as turn context. While a chat turn is held active, queuing a follow-up on the chat resolves the chat rather than a board task and the queued message can be removed, and selecting the provider the chat already uses returns the chat unchanged instead of failing. The chat's own turn state changes (In Progress, then Waiting Response) during a send, and it never renders as a card on the visible Kanban board in any state. A chat turn never triggers the private task-outcome reminders, because the chat is told not to report an outcome; its developer instructions teach it that task language means Playhouse's own board and give it the Playhouse task CLI, and they never ask it to write the page title into its visible answer. Opening a board task while the chat sidebar is showing replaces it with that task's conversation view instead of showing both at once, and returning to the board reveals the chat sidebar again, with the chat's own model left untouched by the unrelated task.

When a standalone chat uses Claude, a missed page signal invokes the Haiku helper at low effort; a malformed result is rejected and retried, an unrelated later question and its assistant reply move to a new titled page, the UI keeps page evaluation visually quiet without blocking the primary answer, updates the transcript separator when classification completes, and holds a following send until the decision resolves, and appends the related follow-up in chronological order. The Claude-specific model and effort arguments are verified through the real CLI/XPC path. An explicit page start during a pending fallback cancels its stale result, keeps the missed turn on its original page, and clears the warning. If all helper results are invalid, the pending decision remains durable, blocks the next provider send, and retries after the helper recovers; the UI keeps the unresolved state visually quiet and sends successfully once recovery completes.

Clicking Stop during Codex reasoning immediately moves the task to Waiting Response and sends Codex's turn-scoped turn/interrupt request. The accepted interruption settles the send without changing the task to Blocked, and a fresh CLI/XPC read confirms the status persisted. A fresh `conversation runtime` read from the daemon reports the turn active and interruptible while it thinks, and interrupted but no longer active once the stop settles. The turn's activity section renders open for as long as the daemon reports the turn active, and folds once the stop settles with no final answer.

Clicking Stop during Claude reasoning immediately moves the task to Waiting Response and sends Claude's session-scoped control interrupt. The accepted interruption settles the send without changing the task to Blocked, and a fresh CLI/XPC read confirms the status persisted. A fresh `conversation runtime` read from the daemon reports the turn active and interruptible while it thinks, and interrupted but no longer active once the stop settles. The turn's activity section renders open for as long as the daemon reports the turn active, and folds once the stop settles with no final answer.

If Codex rejects turn/interrupt while its turn is still active, Stop reports the provider failure and the task returns to In Progress; releasing the fixture lets the original turn complete normally into Waiting Response.

If Claude rejects its session control interrupt while its turn is still active, Stop reports the provider failure and the task returns to In Progress; releasing the fixture lets the original turn complete normally into Waiting Response.

Playhouse opens one main board window titled with its worktree label, displays the transparent theater logo in the board header, uses the same foreground artwork for the Dock AppIcon on a solid #2C2F36 background, and the bridge reports API version 1.

The primary and linked source worktrees resolve to stable, distinct app and XPC identities, build paths, data stores, logs, and managed worktree roots, each worktree root inside its data directory; a saved conversation remains visible after an app restart.

New Task opens with the repository picker closed and composer focused; no selected repository is valid and shows no red missing-folder warning when the required repository root is configured. A standalone conversation can be sent without repository roots, while GUI and CLI reject sends if the configured repository root is missing. The UI and CLI accept standalone sends after the root is configured. The CLI accepts empty-root tasks and rejects blank titles, missing folders, unavailable roots, and invalid merge targets.

A directly created conversation can add repositories in order, edit pending branch settings, and add a context folder; these settings persist across fresh connections without creating branches or worktrees before the first send. The conversation shows the additional context folder without repeating repository worktrees in a Working in summary. Saving an unsent prompt records task creation, prompt save, and subsequent reads with safe argument metadata, result state, and outcome while excluding prompt text.
A selected existing branch remains pending until task start, then reuses its exact existing worktree path.

The conversation picker can add multiple repositories; unset branch settings display defaults and persist pending auto records resolved to local main without creating branches or worktrees before the first send.
A folder-only task persists its context without Git worktrees and reaches Done after a successful turn without attempting a merge.
Adding a repository branch already assigned to another active task is rejected in the new conversation, and the existing task and repository reservation remain unchanged.
Two concurrent CLI/XPC creates targeting the same explicit branch in one repository serialize through a shared cross-process lock, leaving exactly one persisted active task and rejecting the other.

If another process holds the shared task-store write lock when a Codex turn completes after an explicit completed outcome, final status persistence waits and then saves Review status and full history across fresh CLI/XPC reads. Correlated persistence diagnostics include task ID, store path, lock wait, attempts, and retry count; task reads correlate started and completed events by read ID and store path, while failed reads include store file and sidecar state. Reopening the conversation in the UI shows the saved exchange without a store error.

A real ModelContainer open failure against an isolated invalid store path returns an error and durably logs the phase, exact underlying NSError domain/code/userInfo, resolved store path, file/sidecar snapshot, and read-only schema probe failure; the paired visible UI case keeps Playhouse open on its normal board while the same isolated CLI/XPC request fails and verifies the persisted diagnostic.

A real SwiftData fetch failure against an isolated store with a missing task column returns an error and logs a correlated read ID, NSError domain/code/userInfo, store path, file/sidecar snapshot, and the exact missing-column message from a read-only schema probe before the CLI/XPC request completes; the paired visible UI case keeps the normal task board open and verifies the same isolated failure record.

A real legacy SwiftData task store with in-progress timing columns and no submitted-prompt column waits for the store-write lock while CLI/XPC reads concurrently; migration backs up before adding the missing VARCHAR prompt column as nullable with no default and preserves elapsed time at zero. The CLI preserves the task and draft, and the visible app opens the migrated store and preserves the draft through a subsequent restart with duration still zero; metadata advances and later opens create no additional backup. The store is imported once into the protected filename and the legacy database remains unchanged. Committed WAL-only draft data survives import, and a subsequent edited draft survives restart without reimport.

A test-built Playhouse service rejects a data directory outside the temporary test area and a linked store inside it before creating or opening either store; the visible app remains on its isolated board and can still read its tasks.

Tasks with the same automatic branch choice remain pending without creating a worktree before conversation start. When one task has claimed the generated branch, a send from the other (through the CLI, or through the composer, which shows the error and returns the prompt to it) is rejected without creating a worktree and restores the task to Backlog with its prompt saved as a draft and no pending submitted prompt; the opt-in live provider integration sends both turns concurrently and confirms only one task claims the generated branch.

Sending the first message derives an auto branch from the generated task title, with a prompt fallback when title generation fails. Every linked PR must be merged before the task can move to Done. App focus checks each linked PR no more than once per 20 seconds; rapid focus changes are coalesced into one refresh after the cooldown. An unmerged PR keeps its link and suppresses the completion button. PR links and the green completion button have hit targets of at least 30×30 points. After all PRs merge, a later focus check replaces their links with a green completion button; clicking it waits for the task lock and then trusts that already-confirmed merge state, moving the task to Done immediately without re-querying GitHub even if merge status changed while the lock was held. The CLI's task move command has no such cached state, so it always verifies merge status directly with GitHub before completing, including rechecking after waiting for a contended task lock, and reports unmerged pull requests instead of completing when a PR is not actually merged. Completion preserves the source branch and worktree without merging into the local target, retains conversation history, and exposes the task in the searchable read-only archive; the CLI searches matching local Codex JSONL session files, including current input_text and output_text message content, without loading conversation histories, while the visible archive searches both user input_text and assistant output_text, loads the newest 40 first, and reveals older tasks as the user scrolls.
Moving a reviewed task to Done changes only task status and preserves dirty worktree files, branch, and target commit without committing or merging.
The one-time lifecycle rollout clears task records and clean managed worktrees, preserves branches, and retains dirty managed worktrees with a notice.

With both pairs populated, the board keeps Blocked above Backlog and Waiting Response above In Progress, allows vertical scrolling to reach lower backlog tasks, leaves Review as its own column, hides empty status sections, removes Done from the columns, and rejects manual changes to Codex-owned task status; ⌘F reveals and focuses a prominent board search that filters task cards by title as text changes, while close restores all cards. Answering a question without an explicit completed outcome leaves the task in Waiting Response. Task card titles use slightly expanded letter spacing and line spacing.

The CLI publishes standard and custom progress only during an active task turn, persists each report across fresh CLI/XPC connections, rejects invalid reports, and clears explicitly. During an active turn the CLI accepts completed, in-progress, and waiting-response outcomes, rejects invalid or inactive outcomes, and persists the selected status; provider processes started from the CLI/XPC service or the app's composer inherit that app's bridge service name and store directory, and an outcome reported with exactly that inherited environment reaches the task. A successful turn without an outcome receives up to five private status nudges that each offer in-progress alongside completed and waiting-response; a completed report during a nudge moves the task to Review, a waiting-response report during a nudge stops the loop and leaves the task in Waiting Response, and no report after every nudge marks the task Blocked rather than Waiting Response, since the user was never asked anything. The board shows progress details and places completed tasks in Review and waiting outcomes in Waiting Response. New threads receive hidden progress and outcome instructions at thread start, and existing threads receive them on resume; turn requests do not repeat the instructions. Those instructions require updates at phase changes, around substantial tools, and at least every 30 seconds during long work. Only an explicit completed outcome reaches Review. When a final answer ends with the outcome command written as text instead of run, the final answer, fresh history, and transcript hide that command, and it counts as the turn's outcome only when it names this task. Private nudge prompts, replies, and turn-scoped activities remain absent from Codex history and the visible transcript, including after later ordinary turns. Fresh Codex history after those nudges also retains the latest ordinary-turn diff while keeping nudge-only replies hidden.

An in-progress outcome is accepted during an active turn, leaves the task In Progress, and makes Playhouse send a private continuation turn that names the in-progress report; a completed report during that continuation stops the loop at Review. When every turn reports in-progress, Playhouse sends exactly five continuation turns, keeps the task In Progress throughout, and then marks it Blocked with a continuation-limit reason instead of Waiting Response, since the user was never asked anything. Continuation prompts and replies stay out of the visible conversation history. The user taking the work back ends Playhouse's private driving: stopping a continuation keeps the Stop's Waiting Response with no failure reason, and a queued follow-up runs next instead of being buried under further continuations.

Progress reports clear when turns fail or are interrupted and when Codex requests user input; a staged completed outcome is discarded if its turn fails, leaving the task Blocked. The task card removes the report while lifecycle states remain Blocked or In Progress. A blocking structured question appears inline and moves the task to Waiting Response; its answer resumes the active turn in In Progress, and the answered turn finishes in Waiting Response. First-thread instructions distinguish source repository paths from active task worktree paths, allow read-only inspection without attaching a repo, and reserve repository add APIs for changes that need a worktree.
A rename waits for the real per-task operation lock, then persists across fresh CLI/XPC reads; rejecting a blank rename preserves the last valid title.

Root editing preserves order, removes duplicates, rejects an empty list, and waits for an active conversation turn; a stale Git-folder validation is rejected after a newer folder edit, and the newer roots remain saved.

Repository suggestions can be filtered and navigated with Up/Down, and Enter selects the highlighted repository; UI selection waits for an active turn and persists a pending auto branch. While the conversation is empty, a prominent theme-colored heading names all selected repositories and updates as repository APIs add or replace context; compact repository labels remain in the header without a duplicate repository summary. Dark and light themes use distinct prominent title colors, the supporting model prompt sits below with generous spacing, and the generic Start a conversation heading is absent. Additional context folders remain identifiable. The task repository API remains available during an active turn, prepares a managed worktree inside the app data directory's task-worktrees folder, updates saved repository selection, replaces repository context safely, and the paired UI shows API additions/removals. The main assistant is instructed to list repositories through Playhouse, inspect listed source paths read-only without attaching them, and add repositories only when it needs a task worktree for changes or commits.

Pending repository branch, merge-from, and merge-to settings wait for an active conversation turn, then persist across fresh CLI/XPC reads; invalid settings leave prior values intact, and settings are locked after worktree creation.
If a pending repository is removed while its settings are being validated, the stale edit is rejected and the newer repository removal and context root remain saved.

Removing one of two pending repositories leaves the remaining repository in task context and remembered settings, while preserving the removed source repository; the next task restores only the remaining remembered repository. Removing a pending repository preserves other context folders; removing a clean managed worktree through the GUI waits for an active turn, while the task repository API removes it from context immediately and defers clean worktree deletion until the turn releases; a bridge service restart preserves the cleanup intent and a fresh request completes removal; if the active turn writes files before release, deferred cleanup preserves that worktree and its changes; a dirty worktree rejects removal and preserves its task record and files.

The task context menu offers deletion. Pending repository tasks delete without confirmation and preserve the source repository; confirmed deletion waits for an active conversation turn; clean started worktrees can be deleted; dirty started worktrees require confirmation, and canceling preserves the task and worktree. CLI delete-check derives and reports the confirmation requirement from saved task and worktree state without resuming the Codex thread; confirmed deletion removes the managed worktree. Deleting a task also removes its per-task preferences and any left by already-deleted tasks, while another task's preferences remain.

A real worktree-removal failure records the task title and task, thread, process, phase, and underlying error details, including bounded NSError user-info keys and values, without recording conversation text; the failed task and worktree remain available and deletion succeeds after the repository is restored.

The default parent can be read, changed, cleared, and an unavailable path is rejected; a fresh CLI read and repository discovery use the persisted parent. Dark and Light appearance choices persist, the removed PR conflict preference is absent from CLI/XPC and Settings, and appearance changes update the open Settings picker. Clearing the default parent does not change roots already saved on a task.

The configured-root workspace repos list API returns top-level Git repositories while excluding nested repositories and symlink targets. The conversation picker shows those suggestions, filters by repository name or parent path, and reports no matches for non-repository folders.

The CLI reads and writes ordered last-selected repositories across fresh XPC connections; repository batches prepare managed worktrees in order, use task-title-derived branches and main/main merge settings, and set the active task roots to those worktrees. The selected source repository list remains saved and applies to subsequent tasks. Invalid repository paths are rejected without changing the saved preference. In the UI, a new conversation automatically attaches saved repositories in order while the picker stays closed and the composer remains focused. Opening the picker and choosing another suggestion adds it to the ordered context and saved selection for subsequent conversations.

Applying an ordered repository batch with a valid repository followed by an empty Git repository fails without mutation: the CLI reports invalid_argument and fresh reads show no repository attachments or workspace roots; New Task automatically applies saved repositories; an invalid batch shows an error, attaches neither repository, keeps roots empty, preserves the saved order, and leaves the picker closed by default.

The CLI creates an Untitled task with no roots, logs task.create.succeeded for its ID, verifies empty history, and deletes it cleanly. New Task logs start and completion events with the same attempt ID and created task ID, then opens one empty conversation with the repository picker closed, the composer focused, and no create sheet. With no selected repositories, the empty conversation prominently says no repository is selected; typing starts immediately and, with a configured repository root, the UI enables standalone Send. Adding folder-only context leaves history empty, and backing out deletes the pending task without confirmation.

A real directory at the task-store write-lock path makes CLI task creation fail with operation_failed and leaves no task persisted; the paired New Task button shows the save error and writes correlated start and failure diagnostics with the same attempt ID, error domain, and code.

Creating a repository task leaves its selected branch pending while the composer automatically saves an unsent prompt as it is typed; clearing the composer clears the stored draft, backing out needs no Save button, and reopening restores the draft without creating a branch or worktree. Blank drafts cannot be stored, and invalid status changes are rejected without mutation. If the title is renamed while delayed title generation is in flight, the late result is skipped, the renamed title persists, and diagnostics record the skip reason without prompt or title text.

Shift+Enter inserts a newline at the caret without sending and Return submits; multiline drafts persist, expand to the editor limit, remain scrollable and editable across reopening, and submitted prompts persist in history. As content is typed in short increments through successive wrapped lines after a line break, the newest insertion remains inside the visible composer viewport while its internal document follows the caret without scrolling backward. Typed straight quotes, apostrophes, and double hyphens stay literal rather than being substituted. Blank drafts cannot be sent or stored. Sending requires a configured repository root, while a task with no selected repository can still be sent as standalone. If a submitted prompt has no Codex thread or active send reservation after restart, the task returns to Waiting Response, clears its pending marker, preserves the draft, and returns it to the composer. Sending to an Untitled auto-branch task derives its branch from the generated title or prompt fallback before preparing the worktree and starting the conversation; if it is concurrently renamed while title generation is pending, the custom title determines the auto branch. A standalone Untitled task starts and persists its provider thread while background title generation is still pending. Pause remains disabled until the turn is interruptible. Diagnostics correlate title generation with the task and thread while excluding prompt and title text. Queued follow-ups persist with task and thread identity, dispatch after a completed turn, and remain visible for explicit retry after interruption. During an active turn, Return queues a follow-up and queued rows offer Steer. The obsolete footer Queue and Steer buttons are absent.

Selecting text in assistant and user messages shows a floating Add comment hint above and horizontally centered on the selected lines, including wrapped multiline selections; clicking it opens a compact inline comment field positioned beside the hint, with a clearly visible dark arrow on its light submit control. Added ranges render orange and persist after reopening. The composer shows the pending comment count. Structurally recognized comment context is hidden while similar ordinary text remains visible; comments are sent in insertion order with source ranges alongside ordinary composer text. Multiple comments can be added before one send, comment-only sends are enabled, and cancelling the compact field leaves none to submit. Pending comments take precedence over Goal-entry mode: submission sends them to the conversation, exits Goal-entry mode, and does not store the comment payload as a Goal objective. The agent is instructed to start each comment response line with the provider-neutral indexed protocol marker; the transcript renders that marker as a numbered prefix (1., 2.) whose hover opens a medium-sized hint with highlighted text and the user's comment, truncating long values while keeping them identifiable. The serialized payload and ordered response survive CLI/XPC history reload. Legacy Codex markers, response-annotations payloads, and annotation fields still restore their reply details.

A Claude turn that fails after Claude Code created its session leaves that session in place, and the next turn resumes it instead of claiming the same session ID again. After a Claude turn and Playhouse restart, if Claude cannot find its native resumed session, the retried fresh session receives the prior visible conversation from Playhouse's persisted transcript together with the new prompt. Claude completes the turn, and fresh CLI/XPC history and the visible UI retain both turns. A normal Claude resume continues using the native session without receiving duplicate handoff context.

An Untitled Claude task with a pending auto repository branch uses its selected provider to generate the title before worktree creation; the branch and title persist across fresh CLI/XPC reads and the visible task. If Claude title generation returns no title, the prompt becomes the title and branch fallback, and the conversation still starts in that worktree. A fresh `task title` request reproduces the generated title and provider (null when generation yields nothing), and `task reconcile` returns the settled task unchanged.

Claude turns for different conversations run at the same time instead of queueing on a shared turn slot. While one task's turn is held active, a second task's send starts in its own Claude process, runs its own tool, and completes with its own user and assistant messages before the held turn is released. Each turn's process uses its own task working directory, each conversation keeps only its own activity rows and measured durations, diagnostics record no queued-slot event and no prompt text, and the second conversation's answer is available while the first turn is still running.

A failing Claude turn does not disturb a conversation running in parallel. While one task's turn is held and then fails, a second task's send from a separate process completes on its own session and reaches Waiting Response; the failing task keeps its user message, records no final answer, and its provider process exit is the only failure in diagnostics. The UI shows the parallel answer after reopening its task with fresh history.

Stopping one Claude turn pauses only that conversation while a second Claude conversation runs in parallel. The parallel conversation answers and keeps its own activity rows and measured durations while the first turn is still thinking; the stopped task moves to Waiting Response with no failure reason, records no answer, and leaves the parallel task's Waiting Response result untouched. A fresh CLI/XPC read confirms both results.

Two concurrent sends for the same task are serialized across the app and CLI/XPC paths against the local Codex app-server fixture; the second waits for the first, both complete on the persisted thread, the task remains In Progress while a send is active, and successful turns without outcome calls finish in Waiting Response.

When a steer misses its active turn, CLI/XPC and UI accept it into the durable queue for its own turn; opening an empty task waits for the model-aware prompt and omits the generic Start a conversation heading; with no active turn, a missed queued-row steer dispatches synchronously as its own turn and leaves the queue; queued fallback survives process exit or app relaunch and is drained exactly once; a missed regular or queued-row steer arriving during targeted queue dispatch is drained afterward exactly once; a failed targeted turn remains needs-action and does not drain later messages; malformed steer images fail validation; CLI/XPC steering routes image data to a UI-owned active turn and appears in the conversation. Command-Return steers the active turn with attached text and images, then clears the accepted draft and image preview; if the active turn changes before delivery, it clears the draft and queues the complete message for its own turn. Plain Return queues a follow-up; its row Steer uses the active turn ID, appears in the transcript, and removes the item only after acceptance. The obsolete footer Queue and Steer buttons are absent and the active response control is labeled Stop response. Follow-ups persist across reopening, expose per-row Steer, delete, and more actions, and a distinct after-turn follow-up dispatches once after a matching completion and is removed only after successful delivery; removing an unknown queue ID fails without changing the queue.

Backlog draft images persist through fresh CLI/XPC reads and reopening the conversation, with the preview restored; saving more than 8 draft images fails with invalid_argument and preserves the existing attachment. The conversation composer also accepts images from the picker and paste, compresses large clipboard images to fit the 10 MB payload limit, sends PNG and JPEG data URLs through CLI/XPC and to Codex using the tagged image URL payload, reads Codex history image URLs, and keeps earlier images visible after a later text turn and history refresh. The provider-neutral conversation present-image API is included in agent instructions, validates and persists agent-produced PNG and JPEG files as assistant messages, and reopening the conversation renders each image visibly. Diagnostics record image MIME and encoded size without storing image payloads. Clicking a composer attachment, a user transcript attachment, or an agent-published assistant image opens the original image in a large viewer, which can be closed to return to the conversation; a published assistant image preserves the original file bytes.
Malformed image data is rejected with a visible composer error and an invalid_argument bridge response, without creating conversation history or advancing task status.

While a Claude Code turn is active in the app process, the agent's CLI/XPC image publication joins that active Claude transcript turn; after the provider finishes, history places the image before the later assistant answer, and reopening the conversation renders the exact published image. This active-turn attribution is Claude-specific: Codex history is composed from ordered timeline entries, so published images are standalone assistant messages verified for persistence and rendering in test_conversation_sends_image_attachments.

While a Codex turn is active, CLI/XPC image publication avoids requesting provider history; the assistant image is tied to that turn, appears after its native response and before the next turn in ordered history, and remains visible after reopening the conversation.

While a Claude Code fixture turn started by another caller is still running, its commentary and tool activity raise the task's conversation revision in the daemon's runtime snapshot, a held turn with no visible output yet leaves that revision unchanged, and mid-turn history, read from Playhouse's own Claude transcript, already returns the prompt, the commentary, and the in-progress tool activity before any final answer. A conversation reopened after its send, and so no longer reading that turn's stream, shows the commentary and the running tool row while the turn is still held, then the final answer once it settles; the revision rises again when the turn ends.

While a Codex app-server fixture turn started by another caller is still running, its commentary and tool activity raise the task's conversation revision in the daemon's runtime snapshot, a held turn with no visible output yet leaves that revision unchanged, and mid-turn history, read from Codex's native thread while the turn holds, already returns the prompt, the commentary, and the in-progress tool activity before any final answer. A conversation reopened after its send, and so no longer reading that turn's stream, shows the commentary and the running tool row while the turn is still held, then the final answer once it settles; the revision rises again when the turn ends. With a non-default model selected, those mid-turn history reads use the thread the running turn already loaded and never send thread/resume with history's default model.

MCP and dynamic tool lifecycle updates coalesce by stable item ID into distinct visible conversation rows; each call reports its start and measured duration, and completed durations persist through history reload. While a tool call holds the sent turn active, the submitted user message remains visible in the transcript. The latest active process, including a long command, appears outside Working for on one truncated line; older active processes remain inside, and completion moves it inside. The conversation header has no live activity line while responding. Working for renders open while the turn runs, so its progress is visible without a click, and it is still open after leaving and reopening the task mid-turn; every in-flight call is readable from mid-turn history. A collapse the reader performs mid-turn is honored and survives the activity updates that follow, and the final answer closes the section back into a clean collapsed Worked for. The expanded Working for list shows each call's live or completed duration. In-progress, completed, and failed statuses, server/tool identity, and safe result summaries render without duplicate rows, including when later-turn items follow the calls in history. Arguments and raw result text are never exposed.

contextCompaction item/started and item/completed coalesce into one concise timeline event; missing summaries ignore malformed opaque payload fields and never render their data, and the event survives thread history reload with correct prompt/response ordering.

Reopening a 120-message conversation immediately presents only the latest user question, pinned to the top of the viewport with its answer below. Scrolling upward loads earlier messages automatically in 40-message batches, including when the latest turn alone is shorter than the viewport, while keeping the anchored message in place and preserving chronological order. No separate control is needed on systems that report scroll position; below macOS 15 the transcript keeps an explicit Load earlier messages control inside that runway instead. A conversation that was empty when it opened establishes no window and keeps the newest 40 messages rendered as they arrive. Reloading history in place reopens on that same latest turn and keeps upward paging working. CLI/XPC history remains complete and ordered across fresh reads and across an in-place provider switch.

During a parent turn, Working for renders open and active agents appear as individual named rows outside it, with available path/model/reasoning metadata and started-working wording; a mid-turn collapse the reader performs is honored. When the final answer arrives, all agent rows collapse inside Worked for alongside other Codex activity; expanding it reveals clickable agent rows. The UI fixture pauses after the final answer to verify this before turn completion while Stop response remains available. Completed, interrupted, and unknown states survive history reload and remain inspectable after reopening. The child thread opens as read-only through thread/read, thread/turns/list, and thread/items/list without editable controls or thread/resume, and diagnostics retain safe RPC outcomes while excluding conversation text, command output, and diffs. Multiple Codex message deltas and command-output deltas are summarized per item with counts and byte totals, flushed at turn completion, and excluded from individual notification records; lifecycle notifications remain individually logged, and diagnostics exclude conversation text, command output, and diffs. A fresh `conversation subagent-history` read returns the completed child's stored conversation content.

Selecting Plan mode keeps planning active across completed turns and reopening; follow-up instructions start another plan turn, and Start Implementing stays enabled with an empty chat and composer, switches to Code mode, and starts an implementation turn; subsequent composer messages remain Code turns. The plan renders automatically as Markdown with visible spacing, remains selectable and copyable as one complete text view, and CLI events and bridge history preserve the exact plan text and latest implementation handoff. Ordered list items stay on separate lines instead of being merged, and a fenced code block renders as a distinct block with its declared language label and a copy action that places its exact source on the pasteboard. A Markdown pipe table renders as a distinct bordered grid with a header row and data rows instead of raw pipe/dash text, preserving cell content and column alignment, while CLI/XPC history preserves the exact raw table source text. Multiple plan deltas are summarized per item with count and byte totals at turn completion, with no per-delta notification records and no plan text in diagnostics. While the first plan is still streaming in, the question that started it stays pinned near the top of the transcript instead of being auto-scrolled past as the answer grows, consistent with the user message preceding its final answer in CLI/XPC history.

The composer keeps the committed model and effort stable while the picker is open, then updates when it is dismissed. Its popover lists provider models and includes an accessible discrete effort slider with Low, Medium, High, and Extra High choices, constrained by model-reported effort support when available; the visible opaque white knob has no focus border, the 6-point track is visibly thick, and the slider responds to dragging and keyboard arrows. The selected model is global across conversations for the active provider, persists through fresh CLI/XPC reads and reopening, and remains isolated between providers; a saved per-conversation model migrates into the global preference on first read; effort persists per conversation. Malformed model IDs and unsupported efforts are rejected without replacing prior choices. The UI opens a second conversation and shows the global model selection; unsupported modes and malformed model IDs are rejected before creating history.

CLI/XPC Goal set/get/pause/resume/clear persist the objective and lifecycle state across fresh connections and enable the Goals app-server feature; setting the same active Goal preserves its timer generation, clearing then setting another Goal creates a new generation with a fresh baseline, setting a Goal moves the task to In Progress, and invalid blank objectives preserve the current Goal. The UI restores saved Goals; the opt-in live Codex integration confirms native startup, verifies the first Goal retains its elapsed duration, restores a legacy completion without timing metadata, and confirms a second Goal timer begins near zero; renders each achieved summary as a conversation item that visibly moves with scrolling and is anchored to its completing turn, verifies a later user follow-up appears after the prior achievement through turn completion, and preserves both items and their ordering in the read-only Done archive. Native turn activation is owned by the retained GUI runtime.
Claude AskUserQuestion requests with no questions are rejected through the control protocol, fail the turn, and mark the task Blocked; the UI shows the blocked task and its intervention indicator.

Claude's pending AskUserQuestion is persisted and restored from fresh CLI/XPC history after the provider turn ends; the task remains Waiting Response while unanswered, and answering resumes the saved Claude session in In Progress, delivers the answer, hides the private recovery prompt and redacts secret answers from Playhouse history, clears pending state, and returns to Waiting Response. While the recovery turn applying the answer runs, the answered question is no longer pending in history or shown in the reopened conversation, and the task is In Progress; if that recovery dies mid-turn, the question returns for retry with the task in Waiting Response, and answering again succeeds.

A Claude AskUserQuestion asked during a Plan mode turn persists its mode; after its provider process ends, answering resumes the saved Claude session in Plan mode rather than silently downgrading to Code mode, relaunching the recovery turn with --permission-mode plan.

A Claude background Agent/Task call renders a live subagent activity that stays in progress through its launch confirmation and intermediate progress, resolves only once its real completion notification arrives, and keeps the turn open until then instead of settling early. A status-only completion update is not shown as an agent result; the summary-bearing notification is persisted as one normal assistant message in the parent conversation, appears in the visible transcript, and survives fresh CLI/XPC history reads and app reopening without duplication. A failed background agent remains inspectable as a failed activity, and its error summary is not added as an assistant result. When a background agent's notification wakes the parent after its result, the turn stays open through that resumed work, including when the last agent finishes while the woken parent is still streaming, and ends only with the parent's next result, keeping its final answer and both agent reports. A failed agent whose notification the running turn already consumed ends the send promptly instead of waiting for a wake. The system prompt Playhouse appends for Claude lets it run shell commands and agents in the foreground or background, forbids only processes detached with & or nohup, says it can end its response while background work runs instead of waiting and must report the outcome only after the background results, and no longer tells it to sleep, keep shell commands in the foreground, or keep its turn open for work it started.

A Claude Bash call launched with run_in_background stays an in-progress activity after its launch confirmation and keeps the turn open after Claude's result while the shell runs, and still after the shell's notification empties the background task list, until the parent turn Claude Code wakes to deliver that notification sends its own result. The woken turn's answer is the final answer, the outcome it reports moves the task to Review without private outcome reminders, and the shell's completion resolves its activity with the command status without becoming an agent report. When the shell finishes before Claude's first result, so the woken turn starts before that result arrives, the turn waits for both results.

A Claude turn whose result is already out while a background shell keeps it open is still steerable: a queued follow-up's Steer reaches the running turn instead of silently staying queued, leaves the queue, appears in the conversation, and the turn waits for Claude's answer to it before the woken parent turn ends the send.

If Claude fails while applying an answer after restart and echoes the answer or recovery instructions, Playhouse returns a generic error, preserves the pending question for retry while the task stays in Waiting Response, and keeps the prompt out of history, saved task state, and diagnostics.

Codex's pending structured question persists after its provider process exits and leaves the task in Waiting Response while unanswered; Playhouse restores it from fresh CLI/XPC history, keeps provider switching blocked, requires the user to re-enter the secret once, and applies the answers in one recovery turn. The live recovery stream retains safe assistant text while redacting secret echoes; persisted history hides secret recovery responses, provider activities, and file-change diffs. A later non-sensitive Codex turn keeps its own diff and safe response visible in refreshed CLI/UI history while the earlier secret stays absent. In one task, a no-secret recovery response remains visible after a later secret recovery while the secret response is hidden. Secret answers with surrounding whitespace are still redacted when Codex normalizes its echo; the visible UI shows the safe response immediately and after app restart.

When Codex recovery and a later thread-resume/history read error echo the full recovery prompt and answers, Playhouse preserves the pending question while the task stays in Waiting Response, uses a generic visible error, and redacts private content from returned history, saved task state, diagnostics, and error text across fresh CLI/XPC reads and app restarts.

Claude AskUserQuestion requests are delivered through the control path and move the task to Waiting Response while pending; the UI renders the question inline, preserves it across conversation switching, and sends a later answer to Claude before the turn ends in Waiting Response.

A successful Claude turn with an unanswered AskUserQuestion stays In Progress without outcome nudges; after the user answers, the next successful turn receives a hidden CLI status nudge. A question raised during that nudge is rejected through Claude's control protocol with completed, in-progress, and waiting-response instructions, which fails the private turn; both the question and the private rejection instructions stay out of the transcript. Playhouse then stops driving the work and marks the task Blocked naming that reason, rather than spending the remaining nudges.

MCP tool/requestUserInput structured questions raised in Plan mode remain in the conversation and move the task to Waiting Response while unanswered; leaving and reopening the conversation preserves the pending question, keyed answers resume the provider turn in In Progress, and the answered turn reports no outcome, so Playhouse drives a private status nudge; when that private turn cannot complete, the task settles in Blocked naming that reason instead of Waiting Response. A parallel conversation retains its own question and thread; the original conversation receives and answers a second question in its original Plan mode, and completing either conversation preserves the other pending request.

Non-blocking structured questions render inline, remain pending after switching to another conversation, and keep the task In Progress through fresh CLI/XPC history reconciliation after provider exit until answered. Free-text questions expose a selectable Other choice, select it when text is entered, keep it exclusive of listed answers, and deliver the free-text answer through CLI/XPC and visible UI. Answering resumes the provider turn without status nudges while its own pending question is still being resolved; the resumed turn returns to Waiting Response once the pending question clears, and the recovered secret answer stays redacted everywhere.

Async agentMessage questions retain choices and a free-text prompt in live updates and fresh CLI/XPC history, retain accepted-turn model attribution during an active history reload, stay separate from later assistant text, and receive validated answers through the shared manager during and after an active turn. The UI shows inline answer cards instead of raw bullet text, blocks incomplete answers, preserves answered cards across reopening, and displays both submitted answers and responses.

An async question answered after its turn ends stays Pending when the first follow-up fails, rejects duplicate answers across fresh CLI/XPC connections, and becomes Answered only after an explicit queued retry succeeds. The paired UI keeps the card and queue action visible across reopening and then displays the delivered response. A fresh `conversation answered-async` read lists no answered questions while the answer is pending and lists the question once it is delivered.

Turn start persists In Progress; a genuine interrupted outcome remains Blocked with its reason, while restart recovery returns stale In Progress work to Waiting Response with its prompt and conversation available. A saved prompt whose turn never started returns to Waiting Response with its draft intact and can be continued; a turn running when the window quits cleanly or is killed keeps running in the bridge daemon, stays In Progress with its prompt visible after relaunch, finishes, and allows a follow-up. Interrupted outcomes and diagnostics persist across connections; a new prompt can finish in Review. The live turn's activity section renders open and folds away when the interrupted turn settles without an answer, on the conversation that stayed open; the interrupted turn adds no final answer and keeps the activity it reported. A queued follow-up remains visible as needing action after interruption, survives reopening, and is dispatched only after an explicit retry; the completed retry becomes the task's latest saved prompt.

A failed turn preserves its blocked reason and appears in the compact Blocked section above Backlog with a user-intervention indication; retrying clears that section, and the successful retry returns to Waiting Response without an explicit completed outcome.

The task view lists every file changed from the task branch's recorded base in a Changes section below a collapsed Viewed section, including committed branch changes and current staged, unstaged, and untracked edits, and excluding commits unique to the base branch. Marking a file viewed saves its current contents, stages the file in Git, and adds a Viewed entry that keeps showing the reviewed work from the branch base to that snapshot. Work done after that review is listed again under Changes and diffed against the saved snapshot, so one file can appear in both sections at once; a path with no content in the branch base and no current file is zero net change and is hidden entirely, even with a stale viewed snapshot, rather than showing a ghost entry. Selecting text or JSON files opens a calculated side-by-side diff whose header names the baseline used. Viewed snapshots persist across fresh CLI/XPC connections. Files that aren't current Changes entries, including already-viewed and unknown paths, are rejected by the mark-viewed CLI operation, and the UI offers that action only for Changes entries. Uncommitted filenames are green. Opening one diff after another serves each file's own content from the side-by-side editor the app loads once per session, so a later diff reuses that warm editor instead of starting Monaco again. Diagnostics record inventory and file-read outcomes without logging file contents.

A newly created task branch with no branch or worktree changes starts with empty Viewed and Changes sections. External Git commits unique to the task branch and staged, unstaged, or untracked edits update the open task's Changes sidebar automatically; commits unique to the base branch are excluded. Fresh CLI connections report the same per-file inventory.

The CLI confirms a new repository-backed task persists in Backlog; the UI shows no PR control there, then shows the active-card PR action after the conversation completes with a minimum 30-point hit target. The active-card PR control visibly presents its native help on hover; the Done archive PR action remains available with its completed-task label and visibly presents its native help on hover, then waits for the task lock before a real GitHub CLI or branch publication failure without saving a PR link or changing Done status.

The real Git CLI detects merge conflicts without mutation, and PR creation still publishes the task branch and reaches the normal GitHub CLI path; conflicts do not block PR creation. CLI/XPC resolves staged conflicts locally without pushing and commits and pushes a staged resolution without changing the target. The paired UI confirms PR creation proceeds for a conflicted branch and the existing Fix Conflicts action still appears once the PR is linked.

Separate Review task cards probe their linked pull requests concurrently on app focus, with refreshes limited to one per 20 seconds, with focus events during cooldown coalesced into one trailing refresh. A conflicting PR or a mergeable PR whose remote head is not pushed locally retains the imported conflict action with its indicator artwork beside its PR link; the UI renders the artwork inside the action, keeps it beside the PR link, and gives both controls hit targets of at least 30×30 points. Clicking the conflict action sends the corrected request in the task conversation. CLI and UI use the same GitHub mergeability and head checks, retry once when resolution remains unconfirmed, and clear the action only after GitHub confirms the pushed head.

A completed turn outcome on a task with a PR-linked repository and a configured remote commits local work, merges new remote pull request commits, and pushes the branch before the task reaches Review, so the reviewed worktree holds no local-only changes. A linked repository without a publishing remote is left untouched and still reaches Review. When the sync cannot complete, the task moves to Blocked with the sync failure message instead of resting in Review, and a later successful sync pushes the stranded commits and returns the task to Review. While a provider turn holds the task's worktree, the sync command skips it untouched and reports turn-active.

When the remote pull request branch conflicts with local task commits, the review sync merges the remote branch and instructs the task's provider to resolve every conflict; if conflicts remain after the provider turn, the sync fails, the task moves to Blocked with the sync failure message, the merge stays in progress for manual resolution, and the remote branch is unchanged. A rerun with the conflicts staged commits the resolution, pushes the merged branch, and returns the task to Review. The board triggers the same sync automatically when a mergeable pull request's remote head diverges from the local head.

CLI/XPC creates PRs for two repositories, verifies the first PR persists when the second creation fails, retries only the missing repository, confirms each gh create call targets the corresponding repository worktree, and confirms both saved numbers on fresh reads. The UI labels active-card and Done-archive multi-repository creation actions PRs, clicks the active action, verifies the partial-success retry action, confirms the gh create calls target both repository worktrees and retry only the failed one, then shows exact PR numbers on the active task and Done archive, including four-digit values without grouping separators. Hovering the outer padded edge of each PR link triggers its feedback.

Explicit app overrides reject obsolete compatibility metadata, foreign worktree or bridge identities, test IDs that do not match the current worktree, and nonisolated test data before launching; the current app preserves a saved draft across restart.
An invalid legacy database fails import without changing the source or publishing a destination or partial snapshot; the normal isolated board remains usable.

New tasks use the default provider from settings, which starts as Codex and rejects unknown providers, and task create can choose a provider explicitly. A task without a conversation switches providers immediately; provider choice persists across fresh CLI/XPC reads and an app relaunch. Each provider's selected model is global across conversations and persists across provider switches and fresh CLI/XPC reads without reusing the other provider's model. Unknown providers and Done-task switches are rejected, and history has no provider boundary. A Claude task names Claude in the empty conversation, hides Goal mode, and rejects Goal changes through CLI/XPC. Switching a task's provider also updates the sticky default provider for new tasks and chats.

After a completed Codex fixture turn, switching providers is rejected while a follow-up is queued or a turn is active, and the provider menu is disabled during the turn. A settled switch to Claude records a boundary after the last Codex reply that persists across fresh reads and an app relaunch, keeps the Codex thread, and keeps earlier replies labeled Codex; switching back before any Claude turn removes the empty boundary, and the next Codex turn completes in the same thread.

Against the Claude Code protocol fixture, the answer Claude writes before running its Playhouse progress and outcome commands and the closing line it adds afterward form one final answer, not commentary, in the streamed final answer, fresh history, and transcript, and the reported outcome moves the task to Review. Text Claude writes before an ordinary tool stays commentary, and a turn that leaves every status nudge unanswered ends in Blocked. The fixture records all five private nudge attempts for each unreported turn; fresh history hides nudge prompts and replies completely. Switching to Codex hands off the whole Claude answer, excludes answered-turn commentary and private nudge prompts and replies including their redacted placeholders, and hands off only the last commentary from the turn that recorded no answer. A new Claude conversation with no explicit model pick dispatches to Sonnet and shows Sonnet as the picker default.

A standalone chat reports no task outcome, so it ends every turn with Playhouse's own chat page close-turn signal, which Claude runs after its answer and before its closing line. That answer and closing line form one final answer, not commentary, in the streamed final answer, fresh CLI/XPC history, and the visible transcript, so the response is never left buried inside the collapsed Worked for disclosure; text written before an ordinary tool earlier in the same turn still stays commentary there, and the close-turn command really runs and succeeds. This classification is Claude-specific because Playhouse derives each message's phase from Claude's tool stream, while Codex reports the phase in its own protocol and so cannot mis-file an answer on the same turn shape.

The model picker removes the Default entry, superseded aliases, older versions, and duplicate snapshots, keeping only the newest concrete version in each family. GPT-6 Luna replaces GPT-5.6 Luna, and Claude Opus 5.5 replaces the Opus alias and older snapshots. Claude Code names its newest release only through an alias entry's resolved model, so that resolved version supersedes the older concrete Opus 5 and keeps Claude Code's own display name. Alias entries with no resolved model are omitted. A remembered selection the filtered list no longer offers moves to its family's newest offered model and is written back, surviving a later refresh whose list no longer offers that family, while a still-offered selection is left alone. A remembered bare alias migrates to its family's offered release, but a dated snapshot pinned through the CLI is left in place because its family's undated release is not a higher version. The shared CLI/XPC list applies the same filtering to Codex and Claude, and the visible picker matches the Codex list. The model popover opens above its composer control.

The selected effort persists through CLI/XPC reads and reaches Codex turn/start collaborationMode.settings.reasoningEffort; a model's advertised effort limit rejects unsupported requests before history is created. The UI selects Extra High and sends a Sol turn, then simulates a legacy transcript with no Codex turn metadata and sends a Luna turn; the old reply remains provider-only and the new reply is attributed to Luna. The latest reply shows its provider timestamp, while a legacy history item without createdAt has no timestamp label.

Claude's model picker omits Default and aliases, showing Opus 5.5 resolved from Claude Code's bare alias entry as the concrete latest choice in place of the older Opus 5. Selecting it changes the prompt and reply label to Claude · Opus 5.5, and later model changes preserve the old reply's model attribution. The selected effort persists through CLI/XPC reads and reaches Claude Code as CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; the UI selects Extra High and sends a Claude fixture turn whose recorded environment value is xhigh.

Codex and Claude filtered model lists persist across fresh CLI/XPC requests; an unavailable workspace fails refresh without clearing the previous cache. The visible Claude picker shows the seeded cached option before replacing it with the filtered versioned provider list, and retains an offline cached option when the provider executable is unavailable.

A misplaced pending question can be repaired through CLI/XPC only into its owning conversation. Repair rejects a wrong owner and a conflicting destination without mutation, backs up both transcripts, preserves request identity and mode, clears only the misplaced source, and is retryable. Fresh history and the visible UI restore the question only on the original task; answering it clears pending state and the safe response survives reopening. Retrying an interrupted repair after the destination question was answered rejects the stale source without resurrecting the question.

The bridge daemon starts on the first request, serves later requests from the same process, and stays alive while any connection (such as a window's runtime watcher) is open. A watcher receives the daemon's runtime snapshots as a turn starts and stops, and the daemon exits by itself once the last connection closes and no request is running; the next request starts a fresh daemon on demand without any manual step.

When the bridge daemon dies in the middle of a turn, that turn's send fails with a connection error instead of hanging. The next request starts a fresh daemon on demand, which reconciles the task out of In Progress into a resumable Waiting Response, and that daemon can run and stop a new turn.

A task starts with no recorded tokens, and its Token Stats modal says so plainly with no totals shown. Running a real Claude Code fixture turn parses that turn's reported usage into Playhouse's four buckets, adds them to the task's running totals, and records a per-turn row naming the provider and the tools, skills and MCP servers that ran in it. A second turn adds to the totals and appends its own row rather than replacing the first, and the per-tool rollup counts the turns each tool took part in. The task card shows a token usage dot whose tooltip reports the total, and the Token Stats context-menu item opens a modal showing the totals, the per-tool rollup and the per-turn breakdown.

A Codex app-server fixture turn's usage reaches the same per-task totals and per-turn breakdown through Codex's own wire shape, mapping its cached-input bucket onto Playhouse's cache-read bucket and leaving cache-write at zero. The recorded turn row names Codex as its provider, and the Token Stats modal shows those Codex totals in the app.

The token usage color maximum defaults to one million, round-trips through the CLI/XPC settings commands, and rejects a non-positive value as invalid_argument without changing the stored setting. The settings window shows the stored maximum and saves an edited one, and a task card's usage dot re-colors when the maximum changes so the same usage reads hotter against a smaller ceiling.

A newly created Claude task reports cpu-usage as not running before any turn starts. While a real Claude Code fixture turn burns CPU in a real child process, two successive `task cpu-usage` reads establish a baseline and then a plausible non-zero percentage for the task's process tree, the task card's CPU bar reads cool green against the default multi-core ceiling and hot red once the ceiling is lowered to match that load, and the reading returns to not-running once the turn completes.

A Codex task never reports a numeric CPU percentage from `task cpu-usage`, always citing unsupported_provider, because Codex multiplexes every task's turns inside one shared app-server process with no OS-level way to attribute CPU to a single task.

The CPU usage color maximum defaults to one fully busy core per logical CPU, round-trips through the CLI/XPC settings commands, and rejects a non-positive value as invalid_argument without changing the stored setting.
